commands.description:

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation. (user)

commands.description: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. Use when building MCP servers to integrate external APIs or services, whether in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK). (user)

commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (user)

commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill. (user)

commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. commands.name: design-sync

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. const db = await getDb();

- `geometry-admin-router.ts:16` — `'geometry-admin-router'` wasn't a member of the `LogDomain` union. Registered it in `server/_core/logger.ts` next to `'emotional-geometry'`, the same way `'tenant-analytics'` and `'alert-sse'` were added. This keeps the log domain the code intended rather than retargeting it.
- `:327` — `z.record(z.number())` is the Zod v3 form; under v4 the single argument is read as the *key* type, which is why `currentState` inferred as `Record<number, unknown>` and poisoned three downstream errors. Now `z.record(z.string(), z.number())`.
- `:369` / `:405` — `recordPreHook` takes 5 args (the `constrained`/`constraintCount` pair was missing); `recordPostHook` is `(computeTimeMs, loopDetected)` and the two args were passed in the wrong order. Both corrected against `geometry-metrics.ts:187,206`.
- `:379` / `:414` — the advanced neurocosmology hooks want a `CanonicalEmotionalState`, not the flat snapshot. Added a local `buildCanonicalState` helper mirroring the private one in `server/governance/governed-generate.ts:1187` (that one isn't exported, so I didn't reach across to it).
- `:963–971` — `evaluateAlerts` takes a single `AlertEvaluationParams` object and returns a `number`, but was called with 3 positional args (two of them `as any`) and its result read as `result.alertsFired`. Rebuilt the synthetic payload as properly typed `GeometryPreGenerationResult`/`GeometryPostGenerationResult` values and moved the singularity / phase-transition / invariant-violation fields into `neuroAdvanced`, where `evaluateAlerts` actually reads them. Worth flagging: those three fields were previously hung off the pre-result and silently ignored, so `fireTestAlert` could never have fired those three alert types — that's now fixed as a side effect of typing it honestly. The pre-existing `as any` casts are gone; no new ones were introduced.

One thing I left alone, since it's outside this file's scope: `geometry-activation.test.ts:222` asserts `procedures.length === 15` while the router now exports ~40, so that test was already failing before my change. I wasn't able to run the suite to confirm — the `vitest` invocation needed approval that wasn't granted — so the verification here is the typecheck only.
